_note: AETHER Assistant knowledge base. Curated, offline, no model. Every command is a SAFE starter you review before running. Edit freely.

entries.title: Getting started with AETHER
entries.what: AETHER is a learning-first pentest desktop. Open the Security Tools menu (right-click the desktop) to launch a tool, arm Lab Mode before testing, and press Print to capture a finding with a screenshot and note.
entries.caution: Only test systems you own or have written permission to test.

entries.title: Authorization & ethics (read first)
entries.what: Scanning, cracking, or attacking systems you do not own or lack written permission to test is illegal in most places. Always get authorization in writing. Use the built-in lab targets to practice safely.
entries.caution: Unauthorized access is a crime. When in doubt, don't.

entries.title: nmap — discover hosts and open ports
entries.what: Finds live hosts and which services/ports are open on a target. The -sV flag also guesses service versions. Start with a single host you are allowed to scan.
entries.caution: Scanning networks you don't own can be illegal and is easily logged.

entries.title: tcpdump — capture network packets
entries.what: Records packets flowing through an interface, to the screen or a .pcap file you can open in Wireshark. Needs root.
entries.caution: Captured traffic may contain passwords and private data. Handle it carefully and only on networks you're authorized to monitor.

entries.title: Wireshark — analyze packet captures
entries.what: A GUI to inspect live traffic or a saved .pcap. Use display filters (e.g. http, dns, ip.addr==x) to focus. Great for seeing exactly what a protocol does.
entries.caution: Only capture on networks you own or are authorized to monitor.

entries.title: aircrack-ng — audit Wi-Fi security
entries.what: A suite for auditing wireless networks: put an adapter in monitor mode, capture a WPA handshake, then test it against a wordlist. Needs a monitor-mode-capable Wi-Fi adapter.
entries.caution: Only test your own Wi-Fi. A compatible external adapter is usually required on the Pi.

entries.title: John the Ripper — crack password hashes
entries.what: Tests password hashes against a wordlist to see which are weak. You supply a file of hashes and a wordlist.
entries.caution: Only crack hashes you are authorized to test. AETHER ships no wordlists; bring your own.

entries.title: hydra — test login credentials
entries.what: Tries username/password combinations against a login service (SSH, FTP, HTTP, etc.) to find weak credentials.
entries.caution: Noisy and can lock out accounts. Authorization required. Rate-limit and use test accounts.

entries.title: nikto — scan a web server
entries.what: Checks a web server for known issues, outdated software, and risky files. A fast first look at a site you're allowed to test.
entries.caution: Authorization required. Nikto is loud and leaves obvious logs.

entries.title: sqlmap — test for SQL injection
entries.what: Automates finding and exploiting SQL injection in a web app parameter. Point it at a URL with a parameter to test.
entries.caution: Only test apps you own or are authorized to test. This can modify or dump databases.

entries.title: Lab Mode — arm the box (Tor + VPN)
entries.what: One switch. ARMED routes traffic over Tor with a VPN kill-switch so nothing leaks; SAFE is normal internet. Arm it before research, disarm when done.
entries.command: aether-labmode arm   # (aether-labmode disarm to go back)
entries.caution: Strong anonymity is not the same as untraceable. The kill-switch is enforced on real hardware, not in WSL.

entries.title: Anonymous browsing over Tor
entries.what: When Lab Mode is ARMED, open the Anonymous Browser to reach normal and .onion sites over Tor.
entries.caution: Only available when ARMED. See docs/PRIVACY.md for the Tor Browser opt-in.

entries.title: Capture a finding
entries.what: Press Print anytime to screenshot, annotate, and append to your findings log — your running notes for a report.

entries.title: Share files (AirDrop-style)
entries.what: LocalSend sends files to any iPhone, Android, or PC on the same network — no account, no cloud.
